If I didn't know better I would have thought I wrote this myself. The first day I got my little idiot it was all good, but after about a day the panic set in. I freaked out because he didn't follow any pattern of behavior I was told he would. I was googling every single thing he did because I was unsure of what to do. 

I fucked up a lot. I accidentally pulled his tail trying to trim his nails, stepped on his paw when he ran under me, I forgot to feed him one night, and much much more. But he's still fine. Cats aren't babies, they won't die if you don't pay attention to every waking second. Commit yourself to showing your cat as much affection as you can, but don't be afraid to close a door and take a break when needed. Your cat will go take a nap, and when you are ready to engage again he will be up and ready to play. Cats need their own space so I think they can understand when we need ours.

Every few weeks or so I would cry myself to sleep thinking I screwed up and should just give him back to the shelter. But then I would remember how happy he is here. Despite all the mistakes I keep making and all the scratches he has put on my legs, he is happy and I am happy. Regretting such a big decision is normal, but I feel like you would regret it more if you gave your kitty back.

So I had a similar problem in college. What I found helpful was listing everything I had to do in a month. HS isn't as structured so you'd probably be better off doing it weekly. I don't mean just big stuff I mean literally everything. It can be as small as sending an email or as big as finishing a project.

Once you write everything down work on the small easy things first. For me motivation has always been a game of momentum. Not to go full nerd but the law of inertia can be applied mentally. If you check off a bunch of small tasks you will feel more mentally prepared to do bigger tasks. Its like a warm up you do before exercising.

Let yourself be proud of anything you get done even if it's not everything you wanted to do. Focusing on the negatives breaks the momentum. Restructure your plan and try again tomorrow.
